description: Bring a **new** kind of thing into a document: a format, compiled to a real table with real types and checks. Call `formats` first. Each column has a `snake_case` `name`, a `type` — one of `text`, `integer`, `real`, `date`, `boolean`, `enum`, `money`, `link`, `quantity`, `decimal`, `month`, `instant`, `links`, `percent`, `time`, `enums`, `elsewhere`, `file` — and optionally a `unit` (`g`, `kcal`), `required`, `unique` (no two rows share it — a name a row is known by; text, integer, decimal, date, month or link), `values` for an enum or enums, `minimum`/`maximum`, a `scale` for a `decimal` (6 for a rate) and a `note` saying what it means. **A format declares its claims** — `claims`, equations over its numeric columns with a tolerance, like `4*protein_g + 4*carbs_g + 9*fat_g = kcal` within 2%; they make a row provable and never refuse one. **Ask the user whether any figures relate** before answering (a total and its parts, a price and a quantity); a list — books, contacts — makes none, needs no claims, and still gets every refusal. A figure worked out rather than typed is a `computed` column. **`money` is two columns**, minor units beside a currency, so no figure is a float. **`quantity` is two as well**, a figure beside the unit *that row* is in — only when the unit varies by row; otherwise a `real` with a `unit`. Neither takes a `unit`. A **ratio** has a `unit` and a `per` — `density`, `g` per `ml` — the only way a figure crosses dimensions: a claim writes `amount in g via ingredient.density`. No free-text check, no expression. **Across two columns of one row** is a `constraint`, one of four sentences: `isbn is required when kind is BOOK` (`required only when` adds *and empty otherwise*), `at most one of book, article, video`, `score is at most 10 when kind is QUIZ` (or `at least`), and `one row per course, week` (`when status is DONE` limits it) — a row breaking one is refused. `notes` is prose kept word for word: where the figures come from and what was decided. This **creates and never alters**: `extend_format` changes, `connect_formats` joins two. Writes nothing until `commit: true`. **Several at once**: `formats`, a list of these same arguments — links between them resolved in the order they need, all or none.

aggregates.description: What this format works out from the rows of another that point at it. Each has a `name` in `snake_case`, an `of` — one of sum, count, average, minimum, maximum, latest, earliest — an `over_format` and an `over_column` (that format’s `link` column pointing back at this one) or `every: true` for every row of it, a `works_out` expression evaluated on each of those rows **in their own vocabulary**, and an optional `unit`. A `count` needs no `works_out`. A `works_out` may reach one hop through the source’s own links: `amount_g / 100 * ingredient.kcal`. An optional `where` folds only the rows that match — one column of the source, or one hop through its link: `project.active is true`, `kind is not X` (empty passes), `kind is one of X, Y`, `author is not empty`. `latest` and `earliest` read the one row with the greatest (least) `by` — a date, month, instant or integer of the source, `by: as_of`; a tie is unchecked. A claim of this format may then name the aggregate, which is what makes a total something the document proves rather than merely prints.

claims.description: What is claimed about one of these, proved or failed on every row. Each has a `name` in `snake_case`, an `expression` — one `=` with arithmetic over this format’s own numeric columns on either side — an optional `tolerance` (`exactly`, `2`, or `2%` of the right-hand side) and a `note` saying why it holds. Omit when there is none.

columns.description: The columns, in the order they should read. Up to 64. `text` — Words. A name, a note, a code — anything not measured. `integer` — A whole number, with no fractional part at all. `real` — A number that can have a fractional part. `date` — A day. No time of day and no timezone, ever. `boolean` — True or false, and nothing in between. `enum` — One of a list of words you write down here. Each value is any text — spaces, emoji, any language — listed once. A row may send any case; it is stored as written, and anything else is refused. `money` — An amount of money, in a currency the row names. Becomes two columns — minor units and a currency — so it is never a float. `link` — A row of another format. An equation here may read one column of the row it names, and no further. `quantity` — A figure and the unit that row is in — 150 g here, 200 ml there. Two columns. If every row shares one unit, a real with a unit is simpler. `decimal` — A number kept to a fixed count of places — a rate, a unit price. Needs a scale, the places it keeps (1 to 9). Written as a string, "3.5"; extra places are refused, never rounded. `month` — A month, as YYYY-MM. A period, not a day in it. `instant` — A moment, kept in UTC to the millisecond. Written with its offset — 2026-09-23T14:05:00Z. A time with no zone is refused. `links` — Several rows of another format, in order. Written as a list of row names or ids. An equation reads it only by an aggregate. `percent` — A share, shown as 12.5% — a VAT rate, a fee. Typed 87, "87%" or 0.87 — each 87%; 1 is 1%, "0.5%" half of one. Four places. A claim reads 0.87. `time` — A time of day, HH:MM — a shift start. Typed "09:30", "1430" or "2:30pm". end - start of two is hours, past midnight too. `enums` — Several of a list of words you write down here — tags, allergens. Written as a list — ["vegan", "quick"]. Each member is checked against the list, and one outside it is refused by name. `elsewhere` — A row in another document — its path, then the row’s name. Written "F:/projects/site/site.emd S1 U5". Never refused for being out of reach: read back, it says what the row holds now, or that it is unresolved. `file` — A file on this computer, by its path. Or a local app’s address; never http. A `link` or `links` also takes a `target` — the format it points at. A ratio is a number with both a `unit` and a `per`.

commit.description: Write it. Omit or false for the dry run.

computed.description: Computed columns, worked out rather than typed, each `{ name, works_out, note }`: a claim’s expression with no `=` — `price * (1 + vat)`, `amount in g`, `link.column`, an aggregate’s name, another computed column, `end - start` of two times or dates, `due - 3 days`, `due - today`. Money stays money; empty when an input is.

constraints.description: Rules across the columns of one row, each `{ rule, note }` — `rule` is one of `x is required when kind is A, B`, `x is required only when kind is A, B` (and empty otherwise), `at most one of a, b, c`, `x is at most 0 when kind is A` or `x is at least 0 when kind is A`, or `one row per a, b` — no two rows share all of them; add `when kind is A` to count only those rows. `kind` is an enum of this format and the members are its own; a sign goes on a number or money column. Not a claim: a row that breaks one is refused, not reported.

format.description: The name of the format, `snake_case` — `ingredient`. It names the table.

formats.description: Several new formats, each `{ format, title, columns, … }`.

notes.description: Prose about the format. Kept verbatim, never parsed. Optional but wanted.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

rollups.description: Figures per month over this format’s rows, each `{ name, works_out, note }`: `sum of minutes by month of done_on or started_on and project where status is DONE` — sum, count, average, minimum or maximum; `of` one number or money column (none for count); `by` a month column or `month of` a date, one `or` fallback; optionally `and` one link; `where` filters as an aggregate’s, joined by `and`.

rule_sets.description: Rows of this format as rules setting a link of another, each `{ name, sets, note }`: `note.topic from target when title matches pattern by kind (EXACT equals, PART contains) first by priority, recorded in topic_source as RULE, never over MANUAL`. Kinds: equals, contains, starts with, regex. `apply_rules` runs them.

title.description: What a person calls one of these — `Ingredient`.

name: declare_format
title: Declare a new format
